sourcedFrom: SIG SAUER MODX MODULAR PISTOL SUPPRESSOR — OPERATOR’S MANUAL — 8591451-01 REV09 (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: The MODX-9 is a modular pistol can and it fully disassembles: encapsulator, piston housing, piston, piston spring, an O-ring and a stack of individually threaded baffles, all with SIG's two supplied wrenches. ⛔ The single most important habit on this suppressor is WHERE YOU PUT THE WRENCH — SIG warns that unscrewing it by the piston or a baffle takes the suppressor apart instead of taking it off the gun. SIG's minimum cleaning interval is every 1000 cartridges.

steps.title: Clear the pistol, and clean in a ventilated space
steps.action: Magazine out, chamber checked, pistol proved empty before the can is touched. Then set up somewhere ventilated with eye protection on — SIG puts the solvent warning next to the cleaning procedure for a reason, and cleaning a suppressor is one of the higher lead-exposure jobs on a bench.
steps.prose: A pistol can holds more residue than a rifle can, and that residue is what you are about to handle.
steps.quote: READ AND FOLLOW THE MANUFACTURER’S WARNINGS BEFORE USING SOLVENTS OR CLEANERS. USE IN A WELL-VENTILATED AREA. WEAR EYE PROTECTION.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER MODX MODULAR PISTOL SUPPRESSOR — OPERATOR’S MANUAL — 8591451-01 REV09 — 5.2 Cleaning — Warning, p.30

steps.title: ⛔ WRENCH ON THE ENCAPSULATOR — anywhere else and it comes apart
steps.action: To take the can off the pistol, engage a single wrench ONLY on the encapsulator and loosen. ⛔ Put the wrench on the piston or on a baffle and you will disassemble the suppressor rather than unscrew it — SIG states exactly that outcome.
steps.prose: This is the whole trick of a modular can: every joint in it turns, so the one you grip decides which joint opens.
steps.quote: Do not attempt to remove the suppressor by engaging the wrench on any part besides the encapsulator. Attempting to unscrew the suppressor by the piston or any of the baffles will disassemble the suppressor instead.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER MODX MODULAR PISTOL SUPPRESSOR — OPERATOR’S MANUAL — 8591451-01 REV09 — 4.0 Removing Suppressor From Firearm — Note, p.26

steps.title: Piston housing off — one wrench holds, one wrench turns
steps.action: With the can off the pistol, engage the supplied wrenches in BOTH the encapsulator wrench slot and a piston housing wrench slot. Hold the encapsulator still with one and unscrew the piston housing counter-clockwise with the other.
steps.prose: Two wrenches, opposed. Holding the can by hand while you break this joint just spins the whole assembly.
steps.quote: Engage the included suppressor wrenches in both the wrench slot in the encapsulator and a wrench slot in the piston housing.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER MODX MODULAR PISTOL SUPPRESSOR — OPERATOR’S MANUAL — 8591451-01 REV09 — 5.1 Disassembly, item 2, p.27

steps.title: Piston and spring out — and leave the O-ring alone unless it is damaged
steps.action: Take the piston and spring out of the encapsulator, then remove the spring from the piston. ⚠ The O-ring in the piston housing groove comes out ONLY if it is damaged and needs replacing — SIG says so explicitly. Pulling a good O-ring is how you damage it.
steps.prose: That O-ring is what the piston runs against. It is a wear item, not a cleaning item.
steps.quote: Removing the O-Ring is only necessary if the O-Ring is damaged and needs replacement.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER MODX MODULAR PISTOL SUPPRESSOR — OPERATOR’S MANUAL — 8591451-01 REV09 — 5.1 Disassembly — Note, p.28

steps.title: Baffles: hooks in adjacent notches, one holds while the other turns
steps.action: Put the hook portion of both wrenches into the rectangular notches of two ADJACENT baffles. Hold one baffle still and unscrew the encapsulator counter-clockwise to remove it, then repeat the process for every remaining baffle.
steps.prose: Adjacent is the word that matters — the reaction has to be taken by the next baffle in the stack, not by your hand.
steps.caution: Keep the baffles in order as they come off. They go back the way they came.
steps.quote: Place the hook portion of both wrenches in the rectangular notches of adjacent baffles.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER MODX MODULAR PISTOL SUPPRESSOR — OPERATOR’S MANUAL — 8591451-01 REV09 — 5.1 Disassembly, item 7, p.28

steps.title: Minimum every 1000 cartridges — and the rate depends on the ammunition
steps.action: SIG's stated minimum is a clean every 1000 cartridges under normal conditions, and it says outright that the rate of residue buildup varies with what you have been firing. Dirty subsonic ammunition moves that number down, not up.
steps.prose: A minimum is a floor, not a target. On a suppressed pistol the piston is the part that tells you when.
steps.quote: Clean the suppressor at a minimum of every 1000 cartridges.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER MODX MODULAR PISTOL SUPPRESSOR — OPERATOR’S MANUAL — 8591451-01 REV09 — 5.2 Cleaning, p.30

steps.title: Solvent and a NYLON brush or Scotch-Brite — never an abrasive
steps.action: Clean the suppressor threads of residue buildup, then scrub the components with solvent and either a nylon brush or Scotch-Brite pads to take carbon and firing residue off every surface. SIG's approved list is CLP, a suppressor or firearm solvent, a nylon bristle brush and Scotch-Brite.
steps.prose: The approved-materials list is short and it is a list, not a suggestion.
steps.quote: Scrub components with solvent and either a nylon brush or Scotch-Brite cleaning pads to remove carbon and other firing residue from all surfaces.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER MODX MODULAR PISTOL SUPPRESSOR — OPERATOR’S MANUAL — 8591451-01 REV09 — 5.2 Cleaning, item 2, p.30

steps.title: ⛔ BARREL THREADS GET NO LUBRICANT — dry solvent only
steps.action: Clean residue off the pistol's barrel threads with a brush and a DRY cleaning solvent similar to MIL-P-D-680. ⛔ Do not use CLP or any other lubricant on the barrel threads — SIG is explicit, and this is the opposite of what most people do by habit.
steps.prose: Oil on the barrel threads under a booster can is how the can walks loose under recoil.
steps.quote: Clean any residue buildup from the barrel threads with a brush and a dry cleaning solvent similar to (MIL-P-D-680). Do not use CLP or any other lubricant on the barrel threads.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER MODX MODULAR PISTOL SUPPRESSOR — OPERATOR’S MANUAL — 8591451-01 REV09 — 5.2 Cleaning, item 3, p.30

steps.title: Everything dry before reassembly — then moly on the piston
steps.action: Make sure all components are clean, DRY and free of oil or cleaning solvent before anything goes back together. Then the one lubrication point: a light coat of molybdenum grease on the OUTSIDE of the piston every 100-200 rounds, which is what lubricates the O-ring in the piston housing.
steps.prose: One dry rule and one greased part, and they are not in conflict — the moly goes on after the assembly is dry.
steps.quote: Lightly lubricate the outside of the piston with molybdenum grease every 100-200 rounds. This will provide lubrication for the O-Ring in the piston housing.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER MODX MODULAR PISTOL SUPPRESSOR — OPERATOR’S MANUAL — 8591451-01 REV09 — 5.2 Cleaning, item 5, p.30

steps.title: Piston teeth into the encapsulator scallops
steps.action: Slide the piston spring over the piston, then insert piston and spring into the encapsulator — making sure the TEETH of the piston properly engage the SCALLOPS in the encapsulator. If they are not engaged, the assembly will feel right and will not work.
steps.prose: It is an indexed joint disguised as a slip fit. Feel for the teeth dropping in.
steps.quote: Insert the piston and spring into the encapsulator, making sure the teeth of the piston properly engage the scallops in the encapsulator.
steps.cite: SIG SAUER MODX MODULAR PISTOL SUPPRESSOR — OPERATOR’S MANUAL — 8591451-01 REV09 — 5.4 Assembly, item 3, p.34

deepSteps.title: Inspect: threads, baffles, O-ring, and loose residue
deepSteps.action: With the can apart, inspect the pistol barrel threads and every suppressor part for damage, inspect the baffles for damage, inspect the O-ring and replace it if it is damaged, and make sure no loose residue is left in any part.
deepSteps.prose: Four checks, and the last one is the one people skip — loose carbon inside a reassembled can does not stay where you left it.
deepSteps.quote: Inspect the suppressor baffles for damage.
deepSteps.cite: SIG SAUER MODX MODULAR PISTOL SUPPRESSOR — OPERATOR’S MANUAL — 8591451-01 REV09 — 5.3.1 Inspect Suppressor, item 2, p.32

deepSteps.title: The spring test: does the housing move forward with no resistance?
deepSteps.action: The spring can be checked with the can assembled and on the pistol. Pull the piston housing FORWARD away from the pistol: if the housing and encapsulator move forward with little to no resistance, the spring has set and needs replacing.
deepSteps.prose: A set spring reads as a cycling problem long before it reads as a spring problem. This test takes five seconds.
deepSteps.quote: Pull the piston housing forward away from the pistol. If the piston housing and encapsulator move forward with little to no resistance, replace the spring.
deepSteps.cite: SIG SAUER MODX MODULAR PISTOL SUPPRESSOR — OPERATOR’S MANUAL — 8591451-01 REV09 — 5.3.2 Inspect Suppressor Spring, item 3, p.32

deepSteps.title: ⛔ The RIGHT PISTON for your barrel — the thread is marked on it
deepSteps.action: Before installing, confirm the correct piston is fitted to match your muzzle threads. SIG offers several thread sizes and pitches, and the thread pitch and install direction are marked ON THE PISTON. Threading the wrong size or pitch onto a firearm damages both.
deepSteps.prose: Read the piston, not the box. The marking is there because the pistons look alike.
deepSteps.quote: The thread pitch and install direction are marked on the piston.
deepSteps.cite: SIG SAUER MODX MODULAR PISTOL SUPPRESSOR — OPERATOR’S MANUAL — 8591451-01 REV09 — 3.0 Installing Suppressor On Firearm, p.24

deepSteps.title: ⚠ A fixed barrel or an MPX needs its own hardware first
deepSteps.action: The MODX is a booster-equipped pistol can. On a FIXED barrel pistol, fit the Fixed Barrel Spacer before installing; on an MPX threaded barrel, fit the MPX Adapter first. Both have their own sections in SIG's book and neither is optional.
deepSteps.prose: A live booster behind a fixed barrel has nothing to do and everything to batter.
deepSteps.aside: If installing the MODX on an MPX threaded barrel, first see 7.0 MPX Adapter on page 42.
deepSteps.quote: If installing the MODX on a pistol with a fixed barrel, first see 6.0 Fixed Barrel Spacer on page 40.
deepSteps.cite: SIG SAUER MODX MODULAR PISTOL SUPPRESSOR — OPERATOR’S MANUAL — 8591451-01 REV09 — 3.0 Installing Suppressor On Firearm, p.24

cleaning.name: INTERVAL
tasks: Minimum every 1000 cartridges under normal conditions
Sooner with dirtier ammunition — SIG says the rate varies with what is fired
Molybdenum grease on the piston OD every 100-200 rounds

cleaning.name: COMPONENTS
tasks: Suppressor threads cleared of residue buildup
Solvent with a NYLON brush or Scotch-Brite pads on every surface
Approved: CLP, suppressor/firearm solvent, nylon bristle brush, Scotch-Brite

cleaning.name: BARREL THREADS
tasks: Brush plus a DRY solvent similar to MIL-P-D-680
⛔ No CLP and no other lubricant on the barrel threads

cleaning.name: BEFORE REASSEMBLY
tasks: All components clean, dry, and free of oil or solvent
Threads, baffles and O-ring inspected for damage
No loose residue left in any part

reassembly: Baffles back in their original order, hooks in adjacent notches.
Piston and spring into the encapsulator — TEETH engaged in the SCALLOPS.
Piston housing threaded onto the encapsulator, wrench holding the encapsulator.
Correct piston for the barrel's thread pitch, marking read on the piston itself.
Fixed Barrel Spacer or MPX Adapter fitted first where the host needs one.
fncheck: ⛔ Confirm the piston fitted matches the pistol's muzzle thread — size AND pitch, read off the marking on the piston. Then the spring check: pull the piston housing forward away from the pistol; if it moves with little to no resistance the spring is set and must be replaced before the can is used. Confirm the threads on both the barrel and the suppressor are clean, that the barrel threads carry NO lubricant, and that the assembly is seated with nothing loose.
